title: Praveen Kumar Sahu v. State of U.P. — electricity-bill writ dismissed for Clause 6.5 remedy
coram: Sunita Agarwal, J.; Krishan Pahal, J.
disposition: Writ dismissed; relegated to Clause 6.5 engineer.
headnote: A writ challenging an electricity bill dated 16 July 2021 was dismissed because Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is the forum: the consumer must approach the engineer concerned. The High Court did not examine the bill on merits.
facts: Praveen Kumar Sahu invoked the writ jurisdiction of the Allahabad High Court against the State of Uttar Pradesh and three others over an electricity bill dated 16 July 2021. Counsel for the respondents entered appearance. The petition was not heard on the correctness of the demand or on any connected supply-code controversy beyond the existence of a statutory forum. The Division Bench of Sunita Agarwal and Krishan Pahal, JJ. treated the grievance as one for the engineer concerned under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

holding_units.holding: A consumer who challenges an electricity bill in writ proceedings must first invoke the jurisdiction of the engineer concerned under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the writ is dismissed on the ground of that alternative remedy.

principle_tags.application: The writ against the 16.7.2021 electricity bill was dismissed because Clause 6.5 is the alternative remedy.
The Court directed the petitioner to approach the engineer concerned under Clause 6.5 rather than pursue the writ.

not_decided.point: correctness of the electricity bill dated 16.7.2021
not_decided.note: The Court did not examine the bill on merits.
